ssh.title: Remote login (SSH)
ssh.hint: Hop into this server's command line from another computer. Off by default, and only your home network can reach it.
ssh.notInstalled: Off. Flip it and the SSH server gets installed first.
ssh.cantInstall: The SSH server isn't installed, and NoCapOS can't install it on this system.
ssh.offMsg: The SSH server stops and Shield closes its port. Open sessions might get cut. The SSH server stays installed.
ssh.overriddenHint: A settings file the SSH server reads before NoCapOS's own sets: {names}.
ssh.fw.noneHint: Shield's firewall isn't set up, so any device that can reach this server can try to log in.
ssh.fw.offHint: With the firewall off, any device that can reach this server can try to log in, not just your home network.
ssh.fw.onMsg: Shield's firewall starts with a rule that lets your home network reach remote login. You stay connected.
ssh.fw.blockedHint: Shield's rule for remote login got deleted, so nobody can connect.
ssh.fw.fixed: Shield lets your home network back in
ssh.fw.okLan: Open to your home network only.
ssh.fw.okOutside: Open to your home network, and rate-limited from everywhere else.
ssh.connectHint: Type one of these in a terminal on the other computer.
ssh.noAddress: This server has no network address rn.
ssh.whoHint: Root can never log in over SSH. Period.
ssh.passwordOn: Passwords work. SSH keys are the safer move.
ssh.passwordKeys: You've got SSH keys now. Maybe turn password login off?
ssh.guard.sshd: Three tries per connection, and addresses that keep failing get benched for a while.
ssh.guard.fw: Three tries per connection, and Shield slows down addresses that connect too often.
ssh.outside: Allow from outside the home network
ssh.outsideHint: Off: only devices on your home network can connect. On: anyone on the internet who can reach this server can try.
ssh.outsideLocalOnly: This server only lets its own screen open NoCapOS (Settings, General, This Screen & Access), so this stays off.
ssh.outsideMsg: Anyone on the internet who can reach this server can then try to log in. Add SSH keys and turn password login off first. Shield rate-limits the port.
ssh.keys.title: SSH keys
ssh.keys.hint: Public keys that can sign in to your account over remote login, no password needed.
ssh.keys.name: Name
ssh.keys.removeMsg: This key won't get into {user}'s account anymore.
ssh.keys.tooBig: That file's way too big to be a public key.
ssh.keys.othersHint: You're an admin, so you can see and remove anyone's keys.
